scope: Ordered centerline models for the writing lesson inventory. The grader compares pen movement against the selected lesson model; it does not claim to recognize all valid handwriting styles.

sources.name: KanjiVG
sources.method: Extract ordered SVG stroke paths, retain Japanese forms and order, scale uniformly into the practice square. Expanded the existing dataset to cover current single-kanji course vocabulary.

sources.name: Make Me a Hanzi
sources.authors: S. Kishore, project contributors, and Arphic Technology Co., Ltd. (underlying font graphics)
sources.method: 2026-10-26: Extract ordered stroke medians for 1,041 Hanzi used in course vocabulary. Convert (x,y) to (109*x/1024,109*(900-y)/1024), round to two decimals, and store as SVG polylines. PRC stroke order; no Japanese stroke paths substituted. Modifications are freely available under the same Arphic Public License; no warranty.

sources.name: Language Miner print teaching models
sources.method: Original explicitly authored centerlines for Latin print letters, Cyrillic print letters, Greek capitals, and diacritics. Chinese pinyin is Latin writing, including multi-letter initials and tone marks. Shared shapes are reused only within the same print-letter geometry, not across CJK scripts. The displayed order is the selected classroom model; valid handwriting variants can use a different order. Accents and separate dots are written after the base letter.

sources.name: Language Miner Hangul teaching models
sources.method: Original explicitly authored jamo centerlines; syllable blocks compose initial consonant, medial vowel, then final consonant. Horizontal/vertical movements follow Sogang's left-to-right and top-to-bottom teaching rules. Tense consonants and final clusters compose the corresponding jamo; actual lesson inventory is verified separately. No Hanja/Kanji paths or font outlines are reused.

sources.name: Language Miner looped Thai teaching models
sources.method: Original explicitly authored looped Thai centerlines for all 44 consonants and the 14 core vowel units offered by the course. Study the head/loop first, with headless ก and ธ exceptions; preserve upper/lower vowel positioning. The school teaching sheets are reference material only: their images and fonts are not redistributed. The displayed model is one classroom print variant, not a claim that every Thai handwriting style has identical pen lifts.

privacy: Raw pen coordinates are held in memory for immediate grading and discarded on close/profile change. Saved records contain grades, completion, and selected lesson only.
